name: modifier-macro
title: Shared styles as modifier macros
summary: Two style macros, a definePattern whose only child is a modifier list: ButtonStyle (height, pill clip, a fill colour parameter, padding) styles three buttons, TagStyle (no parameters) two tags; each box applies one with an includeMacro modifier, then adds its own ripple and semantics.
prompt: A row of three pill buttons (Save in blue, Share in purple, Delete in red) and two small grey tags (draft, 3 attachments) below, with the button and tag styles each defined once and shared.
teaches: Define a style as a template holding only a modifier list: {"definePattern": {"name": "ButtonStyle", "parameters": ["fill"], "children": [{"modifier": {"modifiers": [...]}}]}}
Apply it with a modifier, among the component's own: {"includeMacro": {"pattern": "ButtonStyle", "arguments": ["#FF4DA3FF"]}}, then ripple and semantics after it
Parameterise only what varies (the fill colour) and keep the rest of the look in one place
pitfalls: arguments is positional and always required, even for a style with no parameters ("arguments": [])
The macro's modifiers are inserted where includeMacro sits in the list, so order still matters: padding in the macro, after its background, pads the content inside the pill

Small savings: about 73 B here (1113 B against 1186 B with the modifiers written out, measured on the one-row version). A macro is mainly for consistency; byte savings grow with the size of the shared list and the number of uses

A row of intrinsic-width buttons squeezes the last one to a sliver on a narrow host: a flow wraps it to the next line instead (a flow ignores spacedBy, so the gaps are spacer boxes, here 54 dp tall to space the lines too)

snippets.note: ButtonStyle: a template whose body is a modifier list, fill as a parameter
includeMacro ButtonStyle with the blue fill
TagStyle: a style with no parameters

check.describe: Three 44 dp pill buttons (blue Save with dark text, purple Share, red Delete) and below them two small rounded grey tags. Resized: the buttons sit in a flow, so on a narrow host (240×190) Delete wraps to a second line instead of being squeezed; the 10×54 spacers keep a gap between the lines. Below about 300 dp wide the widget needs the extra height.
